dek: A Beverly Hills pick service built around lead handicapper Jon Price. The site shows no prices, only a "50% NFL Season Special" and a "Call For Details" investor group. The terms say all sales are final with no guarantees, every record we saw came from Price or from promotional articles, and the start date of the business changes from one profile to the next.

short_answer: Sports Information Traders is a real business with a Beverly Hills address, toll free numbers, written terms and a named lead handicapper, Jon Price. Price has a Wikipedia page (flagged since 2021 for unclear notability), has appeared on sports radio for years, and articles about him run from 2015 to a Gambling911 interview published on 10 Nov 2026. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question that nothing we opened answers. The site publishes no record and no prices, and its picks pages ask for a password. Its free content is daily game previews that, despite "Prediction" in the title, name no pick. Every win rate we found, from "6 Wins, 2 Losses, and 1 Push" to 130 of 160 to a 63% career figure credited to a body we could not identify, traces back to Price or to articles that are promotional, unsigned or labeled sponsored.

The little independent discussion we found is skeptical. In a 2016 Covers forum thread an account writing as Jon Price promoted the service, was asked again and again for a documented record or a contest result, did not give one, and is now shown as banned. Treat SIT as a phone sold service with marketing claims and no checkable record, and note that the terms rule out refunds and guarantees.
pricing_intro: We found no prices on sportsinformationtraders.com on 20 Nov 2026. The packages page lists two offers by name only and sends buyers to the phone line; the menu's "Concierge Service" link simply dials the toll free number. No public price has appeared in any article we read, from 2015 to 2026.
pricing: Features listed: "Expertly hand-picked" and an "Introduction with an analyst to discuss strategy and wager management"; no terms
Features listed: one on one service, access to analysts, picks by text or email; a 2015 Card Player article described syndicate plays with live text alerts
guarantee: The current terms say "ALL SALES ARE FINAL, AND NO REFUNDS ARE PROVIDED," that "credit card payments are non-refundable", that "Consulting fees are fully earned upon payment, and termination of this agreement will not result in any refunds", and "There are no warranties or guarantees regarding our services." They add that the service is "intended solely for entertainment", that SIT's "selections are not guaranteed", and that SIT's total liability is limited to what you paid. Breaking the site rules ends the service "with no refund issued for any portion of Your purchase". Disputes go to Delaware.

That is very different from older marketing. A 2015 Card Player article said the company would "guarantee you'll make money on your investment" and described a "90-day trial investment program", with no written terms. Go by the current terms: once you pay, you should not expect any money back, and betting losses are never covered.

claims_note: How we checked: SIT publishes no record of its own, so we tested the numbers it and its interviews give for internal consistency. The spring 2021 figure works out: 130 of 160 is 81.25%. The BroBible run of 6 wins, 2 losses and 1 push is 75% of decided picks, but nine picks over two weekends say nothing about long run results. A 2015 Card Player interview has Price saying "The key to success is winning between 60-65 percent of the plays"; at standard odds of 110 to win 100, 60% over a season would be a rare result that no public log we found supports.

The start date is not consistent. Wikipedia says Price began selling picks in 2013. A 2017 Hit That Line interview says SIT became respected within "only three years" of offering picks to the public and that Price had profited for "11+ years". A 2023 Bookmaker Ratings profile says he founded SIT in 2002. The site now says he has handicapped for "20+ years". Some of these can be true together, but buyers should know the public pick business itself dates from about 2013 or 2014 by the most specific accounts.

Media claims check out only in part. Wikipedia cites a 2015 Forbes article on Super Bowl prop betting and a 2015 Inc. profile; we found no Wall Street Journal piece, and the 2017 claim of a 5 and 0 week "documented in Forbes" came with no link. Gambling911 credits a 63% career figure to the "LV Sportsbook Commission"; we could not identify any such body, and Price said the real number is higher without giving one.

Contact details vary: the site lists 1-866-704-2001, the terms list 866-356-1232, and the 2017 interview gave 866-441-2711. The site's own counters for "Clients Advised", "Years Handicapping" and "Straight Winning Seasons" were blank on 20 Nov 2026, as they were on 16 Nov.
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for Sports Information Traders plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found none, so there is no Watchdog graded sample for this seller yet.

What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every SIT pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and no third party tracking of the service.

What the seller publishes: on 20 Nov 2026 the Picks and Access Picks pages both asked for a password. The free content is daily betting previews by a staff writer, such as a 15 Nov 2026 Vikings and Packers preview that lists the spread range, injuries and trends for both sides but names no pick, even though its title says "Prediction". No results table was visible anywhere.

Every win rate we found came from Price himself or from articles about him that are promotional, unsigned, guest submitted or labeled sponsored. The newest, a Gambling911 interview of 10 Nov 2026, says the company is "winning at a high level" but gives no figures. Radio segments where he gives free plays are not logged anywhere we could find.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Sports Information Traders pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Sports Information Traders performs.
our_data.context: For scale: SIT marketing talks about 60 to 65% winners and spring runs above 80%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard odds of 110 to win 100 a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Sports Information Traders is thin. Most pages about the service are interviews and features built around Jon Price. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found almost no first hand buyer reports, and the only independent discussion is skeptical. On the positive side sit eight media pieces from 2015 to 2026: Card Player (2015), Gambling911 (2015 and Nov 2026), Hit That Line (2017), BroBible (2017, labeled sponsored), Last Word on Sports (2020, unsigned staff byline), Awful Announcing (2020 and 2021) and a Bookmaker Ratings profile (2023). All repeat figures and stories from Price himself, none shows a log, and some are labeled sponsored or carry no writer's name. The only forum discussion we could open is one Covers promotion thread from 2016: an account writing as Price promoted the service, about a dozen replies asked for a documented record or a contest result and said the Denver call was not bold, and in July one member called him a fraud and said a friend who bought the picks had not come close to 50%. That is one secondhand report in one thread, so it shows skepticism, not a pattern of buyer harm. We found no Better Business Bureau profile, no complaint on any review site, and no court or regulator action.

In the same Covers forum promotion thread, a member who had twice asked for Price's contest record wrote that a friend bought some of Price's picks and "hasn't been close to 50%", and called him a fraud. This is a secondhand account with no record attached, and we could not verify it.

The Covers thread was opened by an account writing in the first person as Jon Price, claiming he called the Denver Broncos Super Bowl run and that SIT clients had a lucrative NFL season. Most of the replies were skeptical: they said Denver was already an AFC favorite, one season proves little, and he showed no documented record or Westgate SuperContest result. In February 2016 the account answered that his clients had been limited by sportsbooks and wished critics luck, calling them "squares". The account now shows as banned on Covers.

A Card Player feature built on an interview with Price called SIT "the premier sports investment service in the world" and repeated his claims of an 8 and 0 run for a poker player and a $200K winnings check. No record was shown, and the page carries no paid content label, but the claims are all Price's.
A BroBible article labeled sponsored followed SIT picks for two weekends and reported 6 wins, 2 losses and 1 push. Nine picks say nothing about long run results.
Awful Announcing reported that Price went 130 for 160 in the spring of 2021. The article gives no source or log for the figure, and the commentary around it comes from Price.

A Better Business Bureau search for Sports Information Traders in Beverly Hills returned no results on 20 Nov 2026. Two Sportsbook Review threads that mention Price no longer opened, and our web searches found no TheRX thread, no review on review sites, and no court or regulator action naming SIT or Price.

Gambling911 published an interview with Price as President of SIT, repeating the site's "big wins, bold calls and unmatched consistency" line and saying the company is "winning at a high level". It gives no record, no prices and no guarantee, and lists the company phone number. It is not labeled sponsored, but every claim in it is Price's.

A Hit That Line interview called Price "the worlds most notable and respected sports handicapper" and let him describe six figure fight bets, "a few hundred clients" and client profits of "tens of thousands to six figures". No log or price was shown.

Last Word on Sports (under a staff byline used for guest pieces) and Awful Announcing (no writer named) ran praise pieces about radio plays Price gave out, a Wake Forest line move and an early season Over call. Neither gives a won and lost record or links to one.

A Bookmaker Ratings profile in Russian retold Price's own stories of a $1 million Super Bowl bet, a $264,000 Royals futures win and a 63% career rate, citing no betting records or regulator filings. It says he founded SIT in 2002, which conflicts with the 2013 date on Wikipedia.

Our saved copy of Reddit betting posts (r/sportsbetting, r/sportsbook, r/SportsBettingPicks and r/nbabetting, Jan 2024 to Nov 2026) held no post about SIT or Jon Price. Fresh subreddit searches in the Reddit archive we use were refused with timeouts on 20 Nov 2026, so this check is partial.

conflicts: The home, Picks and Access Picks pages carry a "Get $1,500 in Bonus Bets" banner that links through a BetMGM partner tracking address (betmgmpartners.com), and an "Exclusive Offer for SIT Clients ONLY" asks clients to sign up with BetMGM through SIT's link. Affiliate deals usually pay the referrer when referred customers sign up or bet. That does not prove anything about the picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
Much of the coverage of Price is labeled sponsored, guest submitted, unsigned, or built on his own interview answers. Read those articles as marketing.
strengths: A named business with a Beverly Hills address, toll free numbers and written terms.
A named lead handicapper with years of radio and press appearances, including a 2015 Forbes mention, so you know who is behind the picks.
The terms are blunt about risk: no guarantees, entertainment only, and the 1-800-GAMBLER helpline.
Free daily game previews give a sense of the research style before any sales call.
concerns: No prices on the site. You have to call, which puts the pricing in a sales conversation.
All sales are final and no refunds are provided, while older marketing promised that clients would make money.
No full public record. Picks pages are password protected and every win rate comes from Price or promotional articles.
The start date of the business, the phone number and the media credits change from one source to the next, and the site's own stat counters are blank.
The only forum discussion we could open was skeptical, and the account promoting SIT there is shown as banned.
Win rate claims of 60 to 65% and higher are far above what verified long run bettors achieve, and the site pushes a sportsbook sign up through an affiliate link.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Get the price, what it covers and the terms in writing before you give a card number. These terms say all sales are final and fees are earned on payment.
Do not raise your bet size because a salesperson calls it an investment. The terms call the service entertainment only.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business with an address, phone numbers, written terms and a named lead handicapper, Jon Price, who has years of radio and press appearances. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because it publishes no record, and we found no court or regulator action involving it.
How much does Sports Information Traders cost?

We could not find out. On 20 Nov 2026 the site listed a 50% NFL Season Special with no price and a Private Investor Group marked "Call For Details". Pricing is given over the phone, and no article from 2015 to 2026 printed a price.
Does Sports Information Traders offer refunds?
No. The terms say all sales are final, no refunds are provided, credit card payments are non refundable, fees are fully earned upon payment, and there are no warranties or guarantees.
Does Jon Price have a verified record?

No. Figures such as 63% for his career, 81.25% for spring 2021 and 6 and 2 with 1 push over two weekends come from Price or from promotional or sponsored articles. His picks pages are password protected and we found no independent log.
What do buyers say about Sports Information Traders?

Very little. The only forum discussion we found, a 2016 Covers thread, was skeptical: members asked for a documented record that never came, and one said a friend who bought the picks was well under 50%. We found no positive buyer report outside the seller's own media.
Is Sports Information Traders worth it?

What you get is picks from a named handicapper with a media profile. What is unproven is whether those picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at standard odds over hundreds of plays. With no public prices, no record and no refunds, a buyer carries all the risk.
